title: Non-defining, Reduced & Advanced Relative Clause Structures
grammarTitle: Non-defining Relative Clauses + Reduced Forms + Advanced Structures
grammarNote: Неопределительные придаточные (non-defining) добавляют информацию о уже идентифицированном существительном. Они обязательно выделяются запятыми. "That" НЕЛЬЗЯ использовать. На продвинутом уровне важны также редуцированные придаточные, конструкция "which" для отсылки к целому предложению, и формальные структуры с предлогами.

grammarTable.subject: NON-DEFINING: who
grammarTable.example: "Kamila, who studies linguistics, presented her thesis." ✅

grammarTable.subject: NON-DEFINING: which
grammarTable.example: "The study, which took three years, was published last week." ✅

grammarTable.subject: NON-DEFINING: whose
grammarTable.example: "Abai, whose poetry changed Kazakh literature, was born in 1845." ✅

grammarTable.subject: Reduced: V-ing
grammarTable.example: "The student presenting her work" = "the student who is presenting her work." ✅

grammarTable.subject: Reduced: V-ed / pp
grammarTable.example: "The report published last month" = "the report which was published." ✅

grammarTable.subject: Which = whole clause
grammarTable.example: "She passed all her exams, which surprised everyone." ✅ (which = the whole fact)

rows.example: "Uralsk, which sits on the Ural River, is in western Kazakhstan." ✅ (not "Uralsk which sits...")
✗ "Kamila, that studies linguistics, is brilliant." → ✅ "Kamila, WHO studies linguistics, is brilliant." ✅

rows.form: 3. The clause can be removed without changing the core meaning
rows.example: "Kamila [, who studies linguistics,] is brilliant." = core meaning intact without the clause. ✅
"Rustam, WHO plays volleyball, is also a writer." ✅ / "The book, WHICH I loved, was long." ✅
"Fleming [already identified by name], who worked at St Mary's, discovered penicillin." ✅

grammarExtra.title: Reduced relative clauses — active and passive

rows.example: "The student WHO IS STUDYING in the corner" → "The student STUDYING in the corner." ✅
"The document WHICH WAS SIGNED yesterday" → "The document SIGNED yesterday." ✅

rows.form: Passive: which + has been + pp → pp
rows.example: "A building WHICH HAS BEEN LISTED" → "A listed building." ✅ (becomes adjective-like)
In formal writing, reductions make prose less cluttered. "Students applying for the programme" is more economical than "students who are applying."

grammarExtra.title: "Which" referring to a whole clause (sentential which)

rows.example: "She passed all her exams, WHICH was unexpected." = the fact that she passed was unexpected. ✅
"The road was closed, WHICH MEANS THAT we had to take a detour." ✅
"The data showed no effect, WHICH SUGGESTS THAT the hypothesis was incorrect." ✅
✗ "She passed, that surprised everyone." → ✅ "She passed, WHICH surprised everyone." ✅
"The country IN WHICH she lived." / "The situation FOR WHICH we were unprepared." ✅
"The professor FOR WHOM I have the most respect." / "The person BY WHOM it was written." ✅
"The country WHICH she lived IN." / "The person WHO I have the most respect FOR." ✅ (natural spoken)

rows.form: Very formal: of which / of whom
rows.example: "The report, THE CONCLUSIONS OF WHICH were disputed..." ✅ (rare; seen in academic/legal writing)
✅ "Kamila, WHO studies linguistics, is brilliant." — NEVER "that" in non-defining. ✅

rows.form: ✗ "The book which I loved was great." (no commas)
rows.example: ✅ "The book, WHICH I loved, was great." — non-defining ALWAYS needs commas. ✅
✅ "She passed, WHICH surprised everyone." — sentential relative = "which" not "what." ✅

rows.form: ✗ "The student studying, who is from Almaty..."
rows.example: ✅ "The student studying is from Almaty." OR "The student WHO IS studying is from Almaty." — don't combine unless you mean two separate clauses. ✅

grammarTip:
Non-defining Relative Clauses:
ALWAYS commas · NEVER "that" · WHO for people · WHICH for things

"Kamila, who studies linguistics, is brilliant." ✅
"The study, which took three years, was published." ✅
"Abai, whose poetry is foundational, was born in 1845." ✅

REDUCED relative clauses:
Active: who is/are + V-ing → V-ing
"The student STUDYING in the corner." ✅

Passive: which was/were + pp → pp
"The document SIGNED yesterday." ✅

Sentential "which" = refers to whole clause:
"She passed, WHICH surprised everyone." ✅
(= the fact that she passed surprised everyone)

Formal prep + which/whom:
"The country IN WHICH she lived." ✅
"The professor FOR WHOM I have most respect." ✅

exercises.text: "Rustam, ___ plays volleyball, is also a talented writer."
exercises.hint: Person + commas = non-defining. Must use WHO (not "that"). "Rustam, WHO plays volleyball, is also a talented writer." ✅

exercises.text: "The report, that was published last year, has been widely cited."
exercises.hint: ✅ "The report, WHICH was published last year, has been widely cited." — NEVER "that" in non-defining clauses. ✅

exercises.text: "She failed the exam, ___ was a shock to everyone."
exercises.hint: "she failed" = whole clause → sentential "which." "She failed, WHICH was a shock." ✅ NEVER "that" for sentential relative. ✅

exercises.text: "The students who are applying for the scholarship must submit by Friday." → "The students ___ for the scholarship..."
exercises.hint: Active reduction: "who are applying" → APPLYING. "The students APPLYING for the scholarship." ✅

exercises.text: "The report which was submitted last Tuesday." → "The report ___."
exercises.hint: Passive reduction: "which was submitted" → SUBMITTED. "The report SUBMITTED last Tuesday." ✅

exercises.text: "WKU which was founded in 1957 is in Uralsk." — Where do the commas go?
opts: "WKU, which was founded in 1957, is in Uralsk."
"WKU which, was founded in 1957, is in Uralsk."
"WKU which was founded, in 1957, is in Uralsk."
exercises.correct: "WKU, which was founded in 1957, is in Uralsk."
exercises.hint: "WKU, WHICH was founded in 1957, is in Uralsk." — commas around the non-defining clause. ✅

exercises.text: "The programme ___ she applied is very competitive." (formal, with preposition)
exercises.hint: "to which she applied" (formal) ✅ / "which she applied to" (informal) ✅ — both correct. "Where she applied" also possible if "programme" acts as location. ✅

exercises.text: "Kamila ___ research was shortlisted for the prize, was delighted."
exercises.hint: "Kamila, WHOSE research was shortlisted..." — possessive non-defining. ✅

exercises.text: "The project was cancelled at the last minute, ___ meant three months of work was wasted."
exercises.hint: "...which MEANS THAT..." — "which" refers back to the whole situation (project being cancelled). ✅

exercises.text: "The essay which she submitted for the prize won first place." — Is this defining or non-defining?
exercises.hint: No commas = defining. "The essay WHICH she submitted for the prize" = tells us which essay (the prize one). ✅
"She hasn't responded yet, WHICH worries me." — sentential relative = "which." NOT "what." ✅

exercises.instruction: Find the non-defining clause without commas error.
exercises.text: "The WKU library which has 500,000 books is the largest in the region."
opts: "which" needs commas — should be "...library, which has... books,"
exercises.correct: "which" needs commas — should be "...library, which has... books,"
exercises.hint: ✅ "The WKU library, WHICH has 500,000 books, is the largest..." — non-defining needs commas. ✅

exercises.text: "Anyone wishing to participate must register by Friday." — This is a reduction of:
exercises.hint: "Anyone WISHING to participate" = "Anyone WHO WISHES to participate." Active reduction: drop "who is/are." ✅

exercises.text: "The report, the conclusions of which were disputed, has been retracted." — This means:
opts: "Both 'whose conclusions' and 'the conclusions of which' are correct"
exercises.correct: "Both 'whose conclusions' and 'the conclusions of which' are correct"
exercises.hint: "...the report, WHOSE CONCLUSIONS were disputed..." ✅ = "...the conclusions OF WHICH were disputed..." ✅ — "of which" is the formal equivalent of "whose" for things. ✅

exercises.text: "The only person who understands this is Kamila."
opts: Defining — "the only person" needs to be identified
exercises.correct: Defining — "the only person" needs to be identified
exercises.hint: No commas. "The only person WHO understands this" = defining — tells WHICH person. ✅

exercises.instruction: Sentential which — which version is correct?
exercises.text: "She finished the marathon, ___ she was very proud of."
exercises.hint: "She finished the marathon, WHICH she was very proud of." — sentential relative (refers to the whole fact) = "which." NOT "that." ✅

opts: Are optional extras always starting with "that"
questions.hint: Non-defining = ALWAYS commas. NEVER "that." Must use "who" or "which." ✅

questions.text: "Kamila, that studies linguistics, is brilliant." — Error:
opts: "that" must be "who" — NEVER "that" in non-defining clause
questions.correct: "that" must be "who" — NEVER "that" in non-defining clause

questions.text: "She passed, which surprised everyone." — "which" refers to:
opts: The whole fact that she passed (sentential)
questions.correct: The whole fact that she passed (sentential)
questions.hint: Sentential "which" = refers to the whole preceding clause. The fact of her passing surprised everyone. ✅

questions.text: "The student ___ research was published is from Astana." (non-defining)
"The student studying in the corner" is a reduced form of:
questions.hint: "The student STUDYING" = "the student WHO IS STUDYING." Drop "who is" for active reduction. ✅

questions.text: "The document signed yesterday" is a reduced form of:
questions.hint: "The document SIGNED yesterday" = "the document WHICH WAS SIGNED yesterday." Passive reduction. ✅

questions.text: "In which" is the formal equivalent of:
questions.hint: "The room IN WHICH they met." = "The room WHERE they met." Formal prep + which = where. ✅

questions.text: Can the clause be removed here? "Rustam, who plays volleyball, is also a writer."
opts: Yes — it's extra info; remove it and "Rustam is also a writer" still makes sense
questions.correct: Yes — it's extra info; remove it and "Rustam is also a writer" still makes sense
questions.hint: Non-defining = can be removed without breaking the core meaning. "Rustam is also a writer." ✅

questions.text: "She hasn't called, what worries me." — Error:
questions.hint: ✅ "She hasn't called, WHICH worries me." — sentential relative = "which," never "what." ✅

questions.text: "The professor for whom I have most respect" — "for whom" is:
opts: Wrong — should be "who I respect for"
questions.hint: "For WHOM" = formal. "The professor FOR WHOM I have respect." = "the professor who I have respect for." ✅

questions.text: When is a sentence definitely non-defining?
opts: When the antecedent is a name or already identified noun
questions.correct: When the antecedent is a name or already identified noun
questions.hint: Name/specific already-identified noun → non-defining. "Fleming, who worked at St Mary's..." ✅

opts: "Uralsk, that is in western Kazakhstan, is an interesting city."
"The report, which I found useful, was long."
"The building, that was built in 1920, is now a museum."
questions.correct: "The report, which I found useful, was long."
questions.hint: "The report, WHICH I found useful, was long." ✅ — commas + "which" = correct non-defining. ✅
